newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Istrabenz says 1996 net slumps.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Istrabenz says 1996 net slumps.

text.p: Slovenian petrol trading company Istrabenz said on Friday its 1996 group net profit slumped to 217.4 million tolars ($1.4 million) from 1.4 billion tolars in 1995.
The company blamed the earnings decline on Slovenia's low petrol prices, which are controlled by the government and are among the lowest in Europe.
Istrabenz, which is 18-percent owned by Austria's largest industrial group OMV and 13.3 percent by the Slovenian state, said group sales rose to 32.4 billion tolars from 24.4 billion.
The company said it had proposed to stick to its policy of paying no dividend, but said the final decision would be taken by shareholders in May.

"We are against a dividend this year because of the uncertainty surrounding the state's policy on petrol prices and because we want to invest as much as possible," Srecko Kenda, deputy general manager for finances, told Reuters.

Shares of Istrabenz, which are listed on the Ljubljana bourse's over-the-counter market, were down 0.36 percent at 2,875 tolars in midday trading on Thursday. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 157.7 Slovenian Tolars)
